steps.title: Our stock in three hospitals
steps.purpose: Read on-hand stock and 28-day use where each hospital keeps it.

steps.title: What FDA wrote at the OAI inspections

steps.title: What our P&T committee already approved
steps.purpose: Read Corvale General's approved interchanges for these items.

steps.title: Which links can't be trusted
steps.purpose: Run the semantic layer's key rules (NDC and unit of use) over each hospital's stock, and name the rows they reject.
steps.finding: 11 stock rows across the system fail the NDC rule; 0 of them are this drug. Every row is in a shared unit of use.

explanation.headline: FDA's records show a warning letter at Hospira, Inc. (FEI 1925262), a plant on our labels, 273 days before the shortage posting

sentences.text: FDA first posted the heparin sodium shortage on 2017-11-14 and it remains current as of 2026-10-21.
The shortage listing includes B. Braun Medical Inc., Baxter Healthcare, Fresenius Kabi USA LLC, and Hospira Inc. as affected companies.
Hospira's plant (FEI 1925262) was inspected on 2017-10-27 and classified VAI, 18 days before the shortage posting.
Baxter's plant (FEI 1025114) was inspected on 2016-02-26 and classified OAI, 627 days before the posting.
Baxter's plant (FEI 2618677) received a Warning Letter on 2017-02-14, 273 days before the posting.
The rule-based best option is to buy from BE Pharmaceuticals Inc., which is not on FDA's shortage list today.
